summary: Five findings against the accepted restructuring RS-28 (Higher local fields as Class field theory, Part II). Two are high: RS-28's own links put FunctionFieldArithmetic and HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory on both sides of each other, creating a two-node cycle in the roadmap graph that is absent from the atlas built without RS-28; and RS-28 reassigns four targets away from FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4, a layer of a roadmap that is neither a member nor an anchor of the family, so scripts/restructure.py never applies the change (it reads roadmaps, layers and links, never owners), FA.4 keeps the mathematics in its own text, and the RS-04 proposal assigns the same mathematics back to FA.4 with an empty 'formerly'. Two are medium: the reviewed library audit records that KTheoryFiniteLocalFields:L.5 owns the logarithmic/DVR de Rham-Witt comparison that HL.2 keeps, and RS-28 lists neither an owners row, nor a supplier, nor a link for it; and RS-28 attributes the characteristic-p differential input to 'the M.5d differential theorem', where MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.5d says in terms that it keeps the Bloch-Gabber-Kato differential theorem separate, and no layer of the atlas owns it. One is low: the claim that the base is the first roadmap prerequisite is not observable in the built atlas, whose prerequisite lists are sorted alphabetically. Everything else checked out: all 96 stage references resolve after retirements, the eight member layers' targets are each kept or supplied, the Part II title reproduces the anchor's atlas title exactly, the twenty-four owner layers own what they are said to, the headline addition is exactly what ClassFieldTheory Layer 8 excludes, and the pinned Laurent-series API exists.
checked: research/blueprint/restructure/RS-28.result.json and RS-28.md in full, against research/blueprint/restructure/RS-28.json (members: HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory; anchors: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory).

content/campaign/HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory/README.md in full: for each of HL.0-HL.7 I matched every 'Construct and export' target against the proposal's 'keeps', 'suppliedBy' or an owners row. Every target is kept or supplied; HL.7 is kept whole.

The anchor: ClassFieldTheory Layers 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11 and 12 read in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_ClassFieldTheory.json. Layer 8 states the exclusion RS-28's headline addition rests on ('Full equal-characteristic `p`-primary existence requires the excluded Artin-Schreier-Witt theory and is not asserted here'), and Layer 12 states 'Every target of this layer is for a number field; global class field theory for function fields is outside this roadmap', which is what makes the FA.4 import at HL.6 right rather than duplicative.

All 96 stage references of the proposal (8 layer ids, 24 owners with their 'formerly' entries, both ends of all 59 links, every 'suppliedBy'): each resolves in data/atlas.json after scripts/retirements.py removes the retired roadmap. None dangles.

The retirement RS-28 relies on: FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration is retired in data/roadmap-retirements.json (2026-09-16, 'A retired roadmap is never a supplier'), so replacing HL.0's documented input FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.4 by LocalFieldsRamification Layer 0 is correct, and LocalFieldsRamification is among that retirement's coveredBy roadmaps.

Each of the 24 owners rows against the named owner's stage description: K2SymbolsBrauer T.2:symbols ('Define Milnor K-theory as the tensor algebra of `Fx` modulo the homogeneous Steinberg ideal'), T.3:symbols (the tame symbol with its sign convention), T.3:localization-comparison ('Develop higher Milnor residues ... construct transfer and prove the norm/residue formula'), T.4 ('Prove the Bass-Tate sequence ... and its transitivity'), CrystallineCohomology CR.4, MotivicEtaleKTheory M.5d, KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.3, FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.2 and FA.4, ProfiniteCohomology Layers 1, 10, 11 and 12, GlobalNumberFields Layer 6, LocalFieldsRamification Layers 0 and 3, and ClassFieldTheory Layers 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11 and 12. All are supported except the two recorded as findings 3 and 4.

scripts/check_restructure.py on the proposal: ok. scripts/restructure.py applied over the 23 accepted proposals in data/restructure/: RS-28 contributes one 'extend', seven narrowings, 58 new stage links and zero skipped links, and no layer of a Tau Ceti roadmap is touched.

The graph, with and without RS-28, after retirements and after applying every other accepted proposal: the stage graph stays acyclic, but the roadmap graph gains a two-node cycle (finding 1). Without RS-28 there is no path at all from HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory to FunctionFieldArithmetic.

Every 'duplicates' entry the reviewed library audit AUDIT-03 (data/library-coverage.json) records for HL.0-HL.7, in both directions, against the proposal's owners, suppliedBy and links. All are resolved except KTheoryFiniteLocalFields:L.5 against HL.2 (finding 3). The remaining unlisted pair, MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.4 against HL.1, I judged a supplier/consumer handoff rather than duplication: M.4 identifies its diagonal with field Milnor K-theory, which T.2:symbols constructs and to which RS-28 assigns ownership.

Section 15 structure: the Part II title 'Class field theory, Part II: higher local fields and higher reciprocity' extends the parent's atlas title 'Class field theory' exactly; the roadmap id HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory is unchanged and the extension is recorded by 'extends' plus a declared roadmap edge; no Tau Ceti roadmap is modified.

The pinned library claim behind HL.0's packaging of F_q((u))((t)) and Q_p((t)) 'from existing one-step valued Laurent series': read at Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174, Mathlib/RingTheory/LaurentSeries.lean line 504 'instance valued : Valued K(X) Z^m0 := Valued.mk' ((PowerSeries.idealX K).valuation _)' and line 824 'instance instLaurentSeriesComplete : CompleteSpace K(X)'. The one-step valued and complete Laurent-series API exists for a coefficient field, so each step of the tower is available; the two-step packaging is not, which is what HL.0 keeps.

findings.where: research/blueprint/restructure/RS-28.result.json, links 3-7 (FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.2 -> HL.5, FA.2 -> HL.6, FA.4 -> HL.6, FA.4 -> HL.7, and HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory:HL.3 -> FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4)
findings.claim: RS-28's own links put FunctionFieldArithmetic and HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory on both sides of each other, creating a two-node cycle in the roadmap graph. After the proposal is applied each roadmap lists the other in both its prerequisites and its consumers, so neither can be built before the other. The stage graph stays acyclic, which is why the guard in scripts/restructure.py (which only refuses a link when the target already reaches the source through stage links) let all five through.
findings.evidence: Applying data/restructure/ with scripts/restructure.py after scripts/retirements.py: atlas['edges'] contains both {'source': 'FunctionFieldArithmetic', 'target': 'HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory', 'kind': 'stage_supported', 'stageCount': 4} and {'source': 'HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory', 'target': 'FunctionFieldArithmetic', 'kind': 'stage_supported', 'stageCount': 1}; the roadmap record for HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory then has 'FunctionFieldArithmetic' in prerequisites and in consumers, and vice versa. All five stage edges are new and carry kind 'restructure' with RS-28 as their only evidence; no stage edge in either direction existed between the two roadmaps beforehand. Control: with every other accepted proposal applied but RS-28 removed, there is no path from HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory to FunctionFieldArithmetic at all (the reverse path exists, through K2SymbolsBrauer).
findings.fix: Remove the single reversed link, HL.3 -> FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4, and with it the owners row that motivates it (see RT-RS-28/2). Equal-characteristic p-primary local existence then stays with FA.4, where the roadmap document and the RS-04 proposal both put it, and HL.3 imports it by an FA.4 -> HL.3 link, leaving FunctionFieldArithmetic a prerequisite of the Part II and nothing more. If instead the proposal really means HL.3 to own it, then the FA.2 and FA.4 imports at HL.5-HL.7 must be rerouted to a layer that does not depend on HL.3, and the change to FunctionFieldArithmetic must be made by the restructuring family that owns it.

findings.where: research/blueprint/restructure/RS-28.result.json, owners rows 13-16 and links 34, 38, 42, 7 (all with FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4 as an end)
findings.claim: RS-28 restructures FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4, a layer of a roadmap that is neither a member nor an anchor of the RS-28 family. It lists FA.4 under 'formerly' for finite ordinary local reciprocity (row 13), the absolute local Artin map (row 14) and the full local existence/correspondence (row 15), moves 'Equal-characteristic p-primary local existence and resulting injectivity/completion of the existing Artin map' from FA.4 to HL.3 (row 16), and adds four new prerequisite edges into FA.4. Nothing applies any of this: scripts/restructure.py reads 'roadmaps', 'layers' and 'links' and never reads 'owners', and the proposal lists no layer entry for FA.4, so FA.4's description is unchanged and still says it proves the local theory itself. The mathematics therefore ends with two owners rather than one, against section 15.
findings.evidence: research/blueprint/restructure/RS-28.json gives members ['HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory'] and anchors ['tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory']; FunctionFieldArithmetic appears in neither. FA.4's description in data/atlas.json still reads 'Specialize and prove the local reciprocity construction for F_{q^d}((t)); then construct the global reciprocity map from ideles, show principal ideles act trivially, and identify every finite abelian quotient by its norm subgroup.' The RS-04 proposal, whose family does contain FunctionFieldArithmetic, contains the owners row {'target': 'Full equal-characteristic p-primary local and global function-field reciprocity', 'owner': 'FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4', 'formerly': []} and gives as its reason for extending the roadmap 'Add completed adelic analysis, full p-primary equal-characteristic reciprocity, zeta/Chebotarev, ...' - the same mathematics RS-28 row 16 takes away, assigned back to FA.4 with an empty 'formerly'. The reviewed library audit AUDIT-03 records the FA.4 overlap against HL.6 only ('Global class field theory for curves over finite fields is this layer's curve case'), and records no FA.4 overlap against HL.3, whose duplicates are ClassFieldTheory Layers 6 and 8.
findings.fix: Restrict RS-28 to the family it is about. Keep rows 13-15 only as a record of overlap, without 'formerly', and drop row 16 and the link HL.3 -> FA.4, leaving equal-characteristic p-primary local existence with FA.4 and letting HL.3 import it. If the programme prefers HL.3 to own it, the FA.4 side has to be decided by the family that contains FunctionFieldArithmetic: add the corresponding 'narrow' entry for FA.4 to RS-04 (and its reciprocal owners row) and reconcile the two proposals before either is applied, since as they stand they contradict each other.

findings.claim: The reviewed library audit records, from both sides, that HL.2's logarithmic de Rham-Witt / wild coefficients overlap KTheoryFiniteLocalFields:L.5, which owns the logarithmic/DVR comparison. RS-28 resolves every other duplication the audit records for HL.0-HL.7 but this one: L.5 appears in no owners row, in no layer's 'suppliedBy' and at neither end of any of the 59 links, while HL.2's 'keeps' retains 'local Artin-Schreier-Witt/logarithmic coefficient interfaces and wild pairings not supplied by the cited regimes' - and L.5 is not among the cited regimes. Two layers are left owning the same comparison, and it is the input on which RS-28's new equal-characteristic p-primary existence at HL.3 depends.
findings.evidence: data/library-coverage.json, layer HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory:HL.2, duplicates: {'layer': 'KTheoryFiniteLocalFields:L.5', 'note': 'Owns the logarithmic/DVR de Rham-Witt comparison for complete discrete valuation rings, overlapping with this layer's wild coefficients.'}; and layer KTheoryFiniteLocalFields:L.5, duplicates: {'layer': 'HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory:HL.2', 'note': 'Introduces logarithmic de Rham-Witt coefficients for complete discrete valuation fields in the wild case, overlapping this layer's logarithmic/DVR comparison.'}. L.5's own stage description in data/atlas.json: 'Import ordinary de Rham-Witt complexes, Frobenius, Verschiebung and restriction from CrystallineCohomology CR.4; own the logarithmic/DVR comparison needed by the calculation here, with its ramification data and map-level comparison.'
findings.fix: Add the owners row {'target': 'Logarithmic/DVR de Rham-Witt comparison for complete discrete valuation fields', 'owner': 'KTheoryFiniteLocalFields:L.5', 'formerly': ['HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory:HL.2']}, add KTheoryFiniteLocalFields:L.5 to HL.2's suppliedBy, add the link L.5 -> HL.2 with that reason, and say in HL.2's 'keeps' that what remains local is the higher-field Artin-Schreier-Witt pairing built on L.5's comparison, not the comparison itself.

findings.claim: RS-28 builds HL.2's wild coefficients on 'the M.5d differential theorem' and gives MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.5d the target 'Prime-power norm-residue and characteristic-p differential comparison'. M.5d states in terms that the differential theorem is not its: it keeps the Bloch-Gabber-Kato theorem separate, and M.5 calls it 'the separate Bloch-Gabber-Kato logarithmic differential statement'. No layer of the atlas owns it - it is named in only those two places and nowhere else in the campaign or Tau Ceti documents - so the theorem underneath HL.2's wild pairings and HL.3's new equal-characteristic p-primary existence has no supplier at all.
findings.evidence: MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.5d, data/atlas.json: 'Prove the compatible Bockstein induction for l^r, filtered-colimit and inseparable/characteristic reductions in their permitted ranges. Keep the residue-characteristic Bloch-Gabber-Kato differential theorem separate.' MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.5: 'At the residue characteristic use the separate Bloch-Gabber-Kato logarithmic differential statement where L requires it. This is not an instance of the prime-to-characteristic theorem.' A search of every stage description and of content/ finds 'Gabber' in the Bloch-Gabber-Kato sense only in those two places. RS-28's HL.2 keeps: '... built on CR.4 ordinary de Rham-Witt and the M.5d differential theorem.'
findings.fix: Replace 'the M.5d differential theorem' by what M.5d does own - the prime-power Bockstein induction and the filtered-colimit and characteristic reductions - and narrow owners row 12 to that scope. Then name a supplier for the residue-characteristic differential theorem itself: KTheoryFiniteLocalFields:L.5 is the layer that owns the logarithmic/DVR comparison (see RT-RS-28/3), and if the Bloch-Gabber-Kato statement is wanted in the generality HL.2 needs, record it as a request against the layer that is to own it rather than leaving it attached to a layer that excludes it.

findings.where: research/blueprint/restructure/RS-28.md ('Put Class field theory first in its roadmap prerequisites') and RS-28.result.json, roadmaps.HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory.reason ('The base is the first roadmap prerequisite')
findings.claim: A reader who opens the atlas will not see this. Prerequisite lists are recomputed from the stage links and sorted alphabetically, so after RS-28 the roadmap's prerequisites begin with CrystallineCohomology and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory is seventh of eleven. What does record the base is 'extends' and the declared roadmap edge, both of which RS-28 sets correctly.
findings.evidence: scripts/blueprints.py, refresh_roadmap_links: 'roadmap["prerequisites"] = sorted({s for s, t in map_edges if t == roadmap["id"]})'. After applying the accepted proposals the record reads prerequisites ['CrystallineCohomology', 'FunctionFieldArithmetic', 'K2SymbolsBrauer', 'KTheoryFiniteLocalFields', 'MotivicEtaleKTheory', 'SchemeAndStackFoundations', 'tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory', ...] with extends 'tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory' and a roadmap edge of kind 'declared' from it.
findings.fix: Say that the base is recorded as the declared base ('extends'), which is how the atlas carries section 15's 'first prerequisite', rather than claiming a position in a list the build sorts.
